15. After the final push, wait for CI and the Codex Bot before sending RESULT.
    - Mark the PR ready for review with `gh pr ready <n>` before the first wait, while it is still a draft (`gh pr ready` exits non-zero on a PR that is already ready, so a later head's wait skips it): the Codex Bot reviews non-draft PRs, and a draft only on an explicit `@codex review` comment. When no Bot review of the final head arrives within 10 minutes, post `@codex review` on the PR and wait out the rest of the window.
    - Run `gh pr checks <pr> --watch` in the background and the Bot wait below at the same time: the 10-minute and 15-minute marks count from `gh pr ready` (from the push, for a later head), never from the end of CI. Right after a push GitHub can report no checks yet, and the watcher then exits 1 with `no checks reported`: start it once a check is listed, and restart it on that message instead of reading it as a CI failure. Wait for that watcher's exit status before the RESULT: a non-zero exit means no RESULT until CI passes.
    - Then list the Bot's reviews of the final head with `gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<n>/reviews --jq '.[]|select(.user.login=="chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]" and .commit_id=="<head-sha>")|[.commit_id,.submitted_at]|@tsv'` and the Bot's top-level review comments raised on it with `gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<n>/comments --jq '.[]|select(.in_reply_to_id == null and .user.login=="chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]" and .original_commit_id=="<head-sha>")|[.id,.original_commit_id,.path]|@tsv'`. A human comment, a CodeRabbit review or an earlier head's review never ends the wait. A comment's `commit_id` moves to the newest head, so findings are matched by `original_commit_id`. Repeat until a review of the final head appears or 15 minutes pass; the report records the latter as `bot: none`. The final head here is the diff head, the last commit that changes the PR's content: a head that only merges the new base with `gh pr update-branch` needs green CI but no new Bot wait. Both endpoints return 30 items per page by default, so keep `--paginate`.
    - This bounded wait is the permitted exception to the no-polling rule in "Regime activation and progress", which governs detecting worker completion and pane status, not a worker's wait on CI and the Bot. List at most every 30 seconds, stop at 15 minutes, and run the loop as a background command or a foreground command with a timeout. Never use bare foreground `sleep`.
    - A 👍 reaction alone is not evidence of a review.
    - Read each listed review's body too: the Codex Bot sometimes places a finding (a `P0`–`P3` badge with a blob link) in the review body instead of an inline thread. Such a review-body finding is listed alongside the top-level inline comments and fixed or dispositioned the same way.
    - Before each fix commit the worker lists every top-level Codex Bot review comment of the PR (`gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<n>/comments`, not only the current head's), every Codex Bot review body that carries a P0 or P1 badge (`…/pulls/<n>/reviews`, attributed to the review's `commit_id`, counted toward the fix cap and the classes, never INV-6's heads, which the gate derives from `review_comment` items only), and the PR's commits (`…/pulls/<n>/commits`), keeps only the comments whose `original_commit_id`, and the review bodies whose `commit_id`, is at or after the task's first commit on the PR (the task.md copy; a reset successor therefore never inherits its predecessor's heads or classes, inline or review-body, which the reset record discharged), and counts two things: the distinct heads after its first RESULT's head that carry a Codex Bot P0 or P1 finding (the rule `scripts/regime-counters.sh` applies: `original_commit_id` of `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` comments whose title carries a P0 or P1 badge, in the PR's commit order), and the finding classes on the PR, from every finding the PR-feedback sweep would list (any reviewer, any priority, inline or review-body; the first three words of each title line, badge stripped, lower-cased), while the INV-6 head count stays the Codex P0/P1 inline `review_comment` items. When the heads reach 2 (INV-6) or a class reaches 3 (plan 006 S1), the worker fixes nothing more: it sends `AGMSG-PONG v1 task_id=<id> status=blocked note=S1|INV-6;heads=<n>;classes=<class:count,…>;threads=<ids>` (the contract's `status=blocked` with everything inside its `note=`, semicolon-separated; no new field) and waits. Before anything review-derived enters a note the worker reduces it: a class name to `[a-z0-9-]` (every other character becomes `-`), a thread id to digits, a Bot title never (only its reduced class), so the note holds only the fixed words `S1|INV-6`, counts, reduced class names and digits, and step 11's inline `agmsg-dispatch` argument carries no review text. The two stops release differently: after an S1 stop the worker resumes only on an ACCEPTANCE that follows plan 006 S1 (the orchestrator's re-examination at `xhigh`, a cause record under `.orchestration/learning/`, and a changed task or plan step), never for a fourth round of the same class; after an INV-6 stop the worker stays stopped until INV-6's own release exists, a reset record naming a redesign by another context or the operator's waiver, never a disposition. The A2 cap of two fix rounds stays; whichever limit comes first ends the fixing. When the heads=2 stop and the A2 cap's third round coincide, the worker sends the `AGMSG-RESULT … bot_rounds=3` that the cap requires, carrying the stop's note fields (`S1|INV-6;heads;classes;threads`), instead of a blocked PONG, and then waits for the ACCEPTANCE: one handoff.
    - Before each push the worker runs `scripts/regime-counters.sh <task id> --history-only` from its worktree and pastes its complete output (the count line, the `detail:` line and any `S2:` line) into its validation file; an `S2:` line there is the same stop.
    - Fix P0/P1 findings, inline or review-body, with a fix commit and start over from the push, at most twice. The third Bot round is not fixed: send `AGMSG-RESULT … bot_rounds=3` with each of its threads listed as `open:<thread id>` (`open:review-<review id>` for a review-body finding), an escalated label that the next bullet's `fixed:`/`not-applicable:` rule does not cover, and the orchestrator decides (a threat-table row, a disposition, or S1).
    - The RESULT names every unresolved thread id with `fixed:<sha>` or a proposed `not-applicable:<reason>`. The worker resolves no thread.
